title: Signal Sweep
premise: A player-controlled echo drone glides across a neon sci-fi grid to recover floating signal nodes before a countdown timer expires.
interaction_model: Touch or pointer drag on the playfield acts like an invisible virtual joystick: horizontal drag turns the drone, vertical drag drives forward or backward, while buttons start, restart, and mute audio.
objective: Collect as many signal nodes as possible while using each pickup's time bonus to keep the run alive.
progression: The game is a single endless-style score attack run that begins at 30 seconds, adds 4 seconds per collected node, increases score with every pickup, and ends only when the timer reaches zero before restarting from a clean state.
theme: Minimalist futuristic signal-recovery mission with holographic UI and scanner-drone imagery.
mood: Focused, sleek, arcade-like, slightly tense, and energetic as the clock winds down.
likely_audience: players who enjoy touch-based survival collection games
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a timer-driven collection survival arcade game.
High confidence that mobile touch input is the primary intended control scheme.
Moderate confidence that the player avatar is best described as an echo drone moving through a signal grid, based on title text and visual language.
Low confidence on any deeper narrative beyond abstract signal recovery, because the implementation is intentionally minimalist.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a mobile-first arcade game called Signal Sweep where the player pilots a sleek echo drone across an abstract pseudo-3D sci-fi grid viewed from a first-person or over-the-nose perspective on a full-screen canvas. The core loop is simple and survival-focused: start with a 30-second timer, drag on the screen like an invisible virtual joystick to steer, use horizontal drag to rotate left and right, and vertical drag to move forward or backward across the world. Floating glowing signal nodes are scattered around the play space at medium distance from the player, gently bob in place, and are collected automatically when the drone gets close enough. Each collected node increases the score by 1 and adds about 4 seconds back to the timer, so the player is constantly chasing pickups to stay alive as long as possible. Keep the world visually minimalist but stylish: a dark neon sky gradient, distant haze, and a projected checkerboard floor grid that sells a retro-futuristic scanning environment. Render the collectible targets as luminous geometric sci-fi markers with cyan, white, violet, and amber accents so they stand out against the floor. Include a polished HUD showing score and remaining time, make the timer turn red and trigger warning audio when it gets critically low, and show a start overlay with clear drag-to-steer instructions plus a game-over screen with the final score and restart button. Add subtle movement bob, collection feedback, ambient music, pickup sounds, and a brief defeat effect. The progression should remain endless score attack rather than level-based: replenish new nodes as others are collected, keep the player moving efficiently through open space, and make the tension come from routing, momentum, and time management instead of enemies or combat.
